# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Delgado**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on the denial letter, or call the number on the back of the insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed]

**RE: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551**

- **Member name:** Rowan Delgado
- **Member ID:** W865123628
- **Reference number:** POC-9391F374E1-41425
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-18
- **Plan:** Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota (Commercial/ACA), state of North Dakota
- **Requesting surgeon:** Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Appeal deadline stated in the notice:** must be received by 2027-02-14

---

## The policy I am asking you to apply

I am appealing under the plan's own medical policy, **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02**, available at https://www.bcbsnd.com/providers/policies-precertification/legacy-medical-policy/c/cervical-fusions. I am quoting that policy below so the reviewer can find each criterion and compare it directly to my records.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a single-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (CPT 22551), issued on 2026-08-18 under reference number POC-9391F374E1-41425. The notice says the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because when I read the plan's own published criteria next to my medical records, my records appear to meet them. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

The policy states:

> "Single or multilevel anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) is considered medically necessary for treatment of symptomatic degenerative disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

I will take the criteria I have in hand one at a time.

**1. Symptoms and neurological deficit.** The policy requires:

> "unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit"

My records document 14 months of progressive neck pain that is not relieved by rest. They also document radicular pain and numbness into my right thumb and index finger with weakness, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. That is unremitting radiculopathy with a documented neurological deficit, which is what this criterion asks for.

**2. Failure of conservative care.** The policy requires that the condition be:

> "refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy"

My records document supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training for **8 weeks**, from 2026-05-18 to 2026-07-13, with **18 visits completed**, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. They also document NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. Eight weeks of supervised physical therapy exceeds the six weeks the policy sets as the minimum, and the therapy, the analgesics and the injection were all tried without lasting relief.

**3. Imaging findings at the level being fused.** The policy requires:

> "complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list. The excerpts I have include these items from the plan's list:

> "Visible loss of disc height compared to adjacent levels with resultant foraminal stenosis"

> "Herniated nucleus pulposus  Spondylosis (i.e., presence of osteophytes)"

My MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-06-26 shows a **C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression**. A disc herniation is herniated nucleus pulposus, and the policy asks for only one item from its list at the impacted level. My imaging documents that finding, along with severe foraminal narrowing and nerve root compression, at the single level proposed for fusion.

**4. Correlation between exam and imaging.** The policy requires:

> "physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion"

My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. My symptoms — pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger with weakness — are on the right side, and the MRI shows severe **right** foraminal narrowing with **C6** nerve root compression at C5-C6. The exam findings and the imaging point to the same nerve root at the same single level.

My records also document that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## A note on what I was and was not given

I want to be straightforward about the limits of what I can address. The excerpts of S-9004-02 that I have reproduced above are the only policy text I have; the imaging criterion ends in a colon and introduces a list of conditions that I have not seen in full, and the policy may list further conditions that are not reproduced in this letter. I have not quoted any plan language beyond the excerpts above, and I have not assumed any threshold, count or duration that the policy does not state in the text I have.

## Request for the criteria the plan actually applied

The plan holds the specific clinical review criteria it used to deny this request, and I am asking the plan to provide them to me in writing as part of this appeal. Please identify the exact criterion or criteria within **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02** that my request was found not to meet, the complete list of imaging conditions introduced by the criterion quoted above, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. The denial notice tells me the request did not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, but it does not tell me which one, and I cannot respond to a criterion I have not been shown. I understand these criteria are published by Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota and can be located through the plan's Medical Policy Search page by searching the CPT code, but the search function does not always produce a working direct link, so I am requesting the applied criteria directly.

## Closing request

I am asking the plan to overturn the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22551 and approve the procedure my surgeon has documented that I need. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies each criterion in **Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02** the plan finds unmet and the specific records reviewed, along with information about my further appeal rights, including any right to an external review.

Per the notice dated 2026-08-18, this appeal must be received by **2027-02-14**. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; anyone reviewing this may also confirm the correct filing location by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.

I am enclosing the records referenced above for the reviewer's convenience:

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-18 to 2026-07-13, 18 visits)
- MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-06-26
- Office and operative planning notes from Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office wishes to include]

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further would help.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Delgado**
Member ID: W865123628
[Signature]
[Date signed]

**cc:** Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
